content: Section 54 of the Act mandates that these entities must, upon becoming aware of a cyber offense being committed on their systems, report the offense to the South African Police Service (SAPS) within 72 hours. Failure to report is itself an offense, punishable by a fine of up to R50,000. This reporting duty creates a direct need for security solutions that provide rapid detection and detailed forensic evidence. The implications of the Cybercrimes Act for a solution like YAL.ai are twofold. Firstly, its advanced detection capabilities can provide the early warning needed for an organization to identify that a reportable offense (such as a successful BEC attempt or malware infection via phishing) has occurred. This enables them to meet the 72-hour reporting deadline. Secondly, the detailed logs, email headers, and attack chain analysis that an advanced platform like YAL.ai can provide are invaluable for the subsequent investigation and for compiling the report required by SAPS. The Act also includes provisions regarding the preservation of evidence related to a cybercrime. The marketing message to financial institutions, in particular, should highlight how YAL.ai helps them meet their specific reporting obligations under the Cybercrimes Act. Phase two should involve a targeted market assault on the financial services and professional services sectors, where the pain of BEC is most acute, leveraging these initial partners.
